summary: I Preterit Intransitive has recurrent result-state story endings, beside resource exhaustion; these are finite forms, with no need to add a box for each closing formula. Added examples favour rarer morphology over further closures.

Preterit-wa tayəmowa (JTM 3.1/21) contrasts with Infectum-wa d̥taymowa (MAC Hanna Dewo/54). The inherited tam-wo example remains in Infectum-wa; surface contraction alone does not settle classification.

III has overt objects and omitted completed activities. Existing III.2 is retained; Hors 2/124 does not independently demonstrate a completed inanimate subject, since a builder with an omitted object is possible.
MAC Ishaq Material culture/76 establishes III Infectum-wa matimíwayle. The proposed Part act. at /74 is withheld because the agreement and referent are uncertain.
Translations at PrS 78/66–67 distribute content across verse boundaries; no new example is quoted from those verses. Several compact records lack source verses.
Parsed III Infectum examples have null sense labels although the contexts resemble III.1. Human-readable counts preserve them as unassigned; no hidden reassignment is made.
Jan Beṯ-Şawoce: the supplied English is project machine translation. All semantic decisions rest on the Turoyo; English quotations are retained verbatim and are not edition translations.
Round 1 had no secure population-destruction sense; Jan adds explicit personal/population patients. The inherited completion sense remains unchanged and numbering continues at III.3.
The l-shaped I forms təmle and təmwole require analysis of borrowing, contraction or analogical inflection. They are not reassigned to III solely for an l-suffix because ma- is absent.

a-vocalism does not by itself establish Preterit-wa: inherited ko-taymo and lo-k-taymi are Infectum. Jan 1.33/1409 is provisionally Infectum-wa from the repeated setting, while tayəmwo (3.14/154) retains Preterit-wa.

Original I Preterit Intransitive and Infectum cells are already full after round 1. No extra closing formula is added. Original III Infectum examples remain unassigned because two inherited senses exist; new III.3 tokens do not silently reassign them.
At Hors 2/124–125 (existing MM 124), is the builder the agent with an omitted object, or is the completed bathhouse the subject?
At MAC Ishaq Material culture/74, what is the referent of lo+tayimo, and is it a finite feminine form or a distinct Part act.? Do not establish the box before this is resolved.
Does islame at PrS 6/33 denote people collectively or their polity? The German specifies Reich des Islam.
At MAC NE Ditin Hazar/6–7, does the carpet never fill up, wear out or reach an edge, and what controls feminine taymo with bread?
Verify source aliases prs 98/2 versus PrS 37/5, prs 207/3 versus PrS 72/56, and MM 124 versus Hors 2/124 before changing citations.
At 65/497, verify edition latla against inherited lat-le; preserve the existing example pending source verification.
At 76/82, is Matiminal segmented matimina l-i arʕo? At 67/99, what noun controls feminine tayimo?
Are final .f in PrS 20/30 and the omissions in the PrS 78/66–67 translations transcription or edition-layout residues?
Confirm the lexical affiliation and inflection of təmle (Jan 2.4/1072) and təmwole (2.12/3045), including whether -le is an affected possessor.
Confirm the two past-box assignments for Taymiwo (Jan 1.33/1409) and tayəmwo (3.14/154), and the exact -wayli sequence in matəmwayli (4.II/709).
In Jan 2.12/2866, is u šərito tayəm already exhausted or imminent? No future form is inferred from the machine translation.
Exhaustion extends across food, wealth, life-force and container contents; these do not require separate end senses.
Container and institution objects stand for contents or work: bowl/coral, school/education and village/stove jobs.
islame is the object in a threat of ending the Islamic collective/polity; a specifically human killing reading is not secure.
Heroes as an inexhaustible collective, friendship, a programme, recording tape and container contents retain ending or depletion.
